title: Software & Data Engineer
description:
Salary: $140,000 – $160,000 per year + bonus + shares

About us

This fast-growing energy software scale-up is helping some of the world's biggest energy players make smarter investment decisions in the energy transition. Their SaaS platform runs sophisticated simulations of energy assets and markets, used by investors, developers, energy majors and consultancies across Australia, the UK and Europe. Freshly funded and expanding into new markets, the engineering culture is pragmatic startup rather than enterprise perfectionism, with one non-negotiable: accuracy. They'd rather a process fail loudly than let a wrong number reach a customer. Work-life balance is modelled from the top down, high performers are recognised quickly through regular promotion cycles and there's room to grow your profile in the energy industry.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and maintain Python data integrations that bring energy market data from around the world into the platform, from clean APIs through to messy flat files and regulator websites

  • Process and standardise high volumes of time series data (prices, forecasts and asset-level interval data) so customers can trust every number in their models

  • Add new energy markets as the business expands across Europe and beyond, extending an existing serverless processing framework

  • Contribute to a newly funded Australian project collecting and processing grid capacity and constraint data, including some spatial data

  • Write well-tested, strongly typed code and help shape how the data platform evolves, including making data accessible to customers through AI-driven tools

About you

  • Experience with ETL/ELT pipelines and both structured and unstructured data stores

  • Exposure to ClickHouse, DuckDB or Glue/Athena

  • Hands-on data processing with Polars, pandas, NumPy or similar, ideally on large time series datasets

  • Solid commercial experience with test-driven software engineering in Python

  • Experience collecting and transforming data from a range of sources, whether APIs, databases, flat file dumps or less structured sources

  • Fluency with typing in Python (pydantic, mypy or similar)

  • Strong collaborative engineering habits: Git, code reviews, automated checks and pipelines

  • A blend of software engineering and data engineering experience

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + an annual performance bonus + share options

  • Annual company retreat with colleagues from across Australia, the UK and Europe

  • One anchor day a week in a central Perth office with flexible, trust-based working

  • Work alongside and report to an experienced Data Tech Lead, with clear technical progression and mid-year as well as annual performance reviews

  • A team that's genuinely leaning into AI and agentic engineering, with premium AI tooling provided


Apply now or reach out for a confidential conversation with Rachel via rachel@analyticsrecruitment.com.au

title: Maintenance
description:
This position is for our Village Apartments of Scottsburg I and II properties. The weekly schedule will be divided between the two properties. This position will be on-call.


Maintenance duties will be divided into daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly categories.

Daily:

  • Walk grounds picking up trash and litter, making sure all traffic areas are free of any hazards.
  • Check dumpster areas for overflowing trash, clean and sweep areas.
  • Check common areas for trash and empty any trash containers on site.
  • Public restrooms should be checked and any toiletry supplies refilled
  • Check laundry rooms
  • Check for any new work orders in the maintenance box or with the site management.

Weekly:

  • Clean dumpster area.
  • Clean common areas, hallways, restrooms, laundry room.
  • Blow off or sweep parking lots
  • Make sure all weeds are pulled and sprayed with weed killer.
  • Check all landscaping to see if trimming is needed.
  • Check all vacant units, do necessary steps to get rent ready.
  • Check site lighting after dark to make sure everything is working properly.
  • Complete work orders.

Monthly:

  • Deep clean laundry room.
  • Wash common area windows as needed.
  • Clean out all light fixtures of bugs and debris.
  • Clean and organize maintenance areas.
  • Change filters on any common area HVAC units.
  • Check any common area smoke alarms.

Quarterly:

  • Assist site manager with quarterly inspections of units, replace all furnace filters.
  • Check gutters and downspouts for debris. If you have a 2 story (or higher) building, hire out.

Note: Should a need arise to have an independent contractor perform a maintenance repair, the maintenance person shall inform the Property Manager before the repair is done.

title: Senior Dynamics 365 Functional Consultant
description:
About the Company

Our client is a leading organisation within the financial services industry, with a strong focus on delivering high-quality services and experiences to its customers. As part of an ongoing technology uplift, they are strengthening internal ownership of their CRM and contact-centre environment and investing in the optimisation of their Microsoft Dynamics 365 platform.

About the Role

An opportunity is available for a Senior Dynamics 365 Functional Consultant to take a key role in stabilising, optimising and improving an established Dynamics 365 CRM environment.




Working across business and technology teams, you will assess the existing platform, identify improvement opportunities and translate business requirements into practical, sustainable CRM solutions. You will provide functional solution design expertise across Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Dataverse and Power Platform, while supporting integrations with the organisation's contact-centre technology.




A key focus will be improving the interaction between Dynamics 365 and Amazon Connect, ensuring customer interactions, cases and data flow effectively between platforms.




You will also act as an internal Dynamics 365 SME, providing design guidance, challenging vendor recommendations where appropriate and helping establish stronger internal ownership and governance of the CRM platform.




Key responsibilities will include:

  • Assess and optimise the existing Dynamics 365 CRM environment.
  • Develop functional and solution designs for CRM improvements.
  • Translate business requirements into user stories, process designs and acceptance criteria.
  • Support Dynamics 365, Dataverse and contact-centre integrations.
  • Investigate recurring platform, data and integration issues.
  • Support testing, defect management and release readiness.
  • Review vendor solutions and provide functional design assurance.
  • Improve CRM processes, data quality, adoption and ways of working.
  • Contribute to CRM governance, standards and platform ownership.

About You

You will be an experienced Dynamics 365 Functional Consultant with strong hands-on CRM knowledge and the ability to bridge business requirements and technical solution delivery.




You will ideally bring:

  • Strong Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM functional experience.
  • Experience with Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
  • Strong knowledge of Dataverse, including tables, relationships, security, workflows, forms and views.
  • Experience designing and configuring Dynamics 365 solutions.
  • Microsoft Power Platform experience, including Power Apps and Power Automate.
  • Experience with CRM integrations, APIs and data mapping.
  • Exposure to contact-centre or telephony integrations, ideally Amazon Connect.
  • Experience with functional testing, UAT and defect management.
  • Strong stakeholder and vendor-management capabilities.
  • The ability to assess existing solutions and recommend practical improvements.
  • Superannuation industry experience will be highly regarded.

This is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of a significant Dynamics 365 environment, influence how the platform evolves and help build sustainable internal CRM capability.

Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Dylan Tasker on dylan.tasker@davidsonwp.com , quoting reference JN -092026-44200. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

title: Data and AI Automation Specialist
description:
Job Details

Application Open: Full-Time

Job Purpose:

The Data and AI Automation Specialist is embedded within the Division of Computing and Mathematical Sciences (CMS) and holds two closely connected responsibilities. The first is to transform academic, student, faculty, research, and operational data into reliable evidence for divisional planning and decision making. The second is to design, build, and maintain the automated and agentic AI workflows that put that evidence, and other routine university processes, to work. The role works closely with CMS leadership, faculty, program administrators, and professional staff to collect, validate, analyze, interpret, and communicate information that supports teaching quality, student success, program development, research performance, resource planning, accreditation, and continuous improvement. This is a hands-on building role as well as an analytical one: the specialist is expected to construct, test, document, and operate working automations and agentic AI solutions in low code platforms such as KNIME and n8n, rather than only specifying them for others to build. The specialist will work in close partnership with Institutional Research to align definitions, methods, governance, and reporting with university standards and authoritative data sources, and with Information Technology on integration, access, and safe deployment. The role also serves as the business analysis partner for faculty led AI initiatives that support university operations, translating operational needs into clear requirements, identifying suitable and authoritative data sources, assessing data quality and readiness, and providing analytical and practical AI support throughout solution development and evaluation.

Key Responsibilities:

Academic and divisional data analysis

  • Collect, integrate, clean, validate, and analyze quantitative and qualitative data relevant to CMS programs, courses, students, faculty, research, and operations.
  • Analyze curriculum delivery, course demand, teaching activity, student outcomes, faculty workload, research productivity, and resource utilization to provide evidence for curriculum planning, course scheduling, student success initiatives, faculty and resource planning, program review, and continuous improvement.
  • Apply appropriate statistical methods, trend analysis, forecasting, segmentation, and predictive techniques to identify patterns, risks, and opportunities within CMS.
  • Investigate data anomalies, reconcile conflicting sources with relevant data owners and Institutional Research, and document assumptions and limitations before results are released.

Divisional reporting, dashboards, and decision support

  • Develop and maintain recurring CMS reports, profiles, scorecards, and interactive dashboards for the Division leadership, committees, faculty, and authorized university stakeholders.
  • Translate complex academic, research, and operational findings into concise narratives, visualizations, presentations, and recommendations for technical and nontechnical audiences, highlighting material changes, risks, emerging issues, and implications for leadership and committee decision-making.
  • Respond to approved CMS information requests using clear definitions, reproducible methods, appropriate access controls, and documented quality checks.
  • Automate repeatable data preparation and reporting activities to improve the timeliness, consistency, and scalability of CMS analytics.

Program quality, accreditation, and university reporting

  • Compile and verify CMS evidence for program accreditation, academic program review, curriculum review, and quality assurance activities.
  • Maintain reporting calendars, supporting documentation, audit trails, and source records for CMS data products and submissions.
  • Interpret academic and external reporting requirements with Institutional Research, identify CMS data gaps, and work with relevant owners to resolve them.

Academic planning and performance improvement

  • Benchmark CMS programs, disciplines, and performance against relevant local and international peers using comparable definitions and defensible indicators.
  • Research developments and good practice in academic analytics, computing and mathematical sciences education, research performance, and data management.
  • Support the design, monitoring, and review of divisional key performance indicators and measures aligned with CMS and University priorities.

Data governance and cross university collaboration

  • Serve as the primary analytical liaison between CMS and Institutional Research, coordinating with Institutional Research and other University offices to ensure accurate and timely CMS data for regulatory submissions, rankings, surveys, approved external reporting, and other institutional requirements.
  • Maintain CMS data dictionaries, metric definitions, reporting specifications, business rules, and standard operating procedures in alignment with university standards.
  • Apply university policies and applicable requirements for privacy, confidentiality, access control, retention, and the ethical use of academic and research data, including the use of third-party AI services.
  • Promote consistent use of authoritative data sources and collaborate with Institutional Research and Information Technology to strengthen data quality, system design, and reporting practices.
  • Build trusted relationships across CMS and provide practical guidance to faculty and staff on interpreting and using divisional data and AI enabled tools.

Workflow automation and agentic AI development

  • Design, build, test, document, and maintain end to end data and process automations using low code workflow platforms such as KNIME and n8n, covering scheduled data pipelines, validation routines, alerting, and the preparation and distribution of recurring reports.
  • Build and operate agentic AI workflows that combine large language models with university data sources, APIs, and tools to support tasks such as document summarization, information retrieval, classification and routing, drafting, extraction of structured data from unstructured sources, and first line handling of routine requests.
  • Integrate workflows with university systems and services through APIs, webhooks, databases, file stores, email, and collaboration platforms, working with Information Technology on authentication, permissions, environments, and safe deployment.
  • Apply sound engineering practice to automation, including version control, separation of development and production environments, parameterization and reuse, error handling, retry and fallback logic, logging, and monitoring.
  • Define and run evaluation for AI enabled workflows, including representative test sets, accuracy and quality measures, failure analysis, cost and latency tracking, and regression testing before and after changes.
  • Design human in the loop controls, approval steps, escalation paths, and explicit boundaries for autonomous action, so that agents operate only within approved limits and failures are detected early.
  • Maintain a register of divisional automations and agents for recording purpose, owner, data used, systems touched, dependencies, review dates, and decommissioning plans.
  • Document the data flow of each automation and agent, including which data leaves university systems, where it is processed, what is logged, and how long it is retained, and raise any concerns before deployment.
  • Prototype quickly, demonstrate working solutions to stakeholders, advance the ones that prove their value from pilot to supported operation, and retire those that do not.
  • Provide practical enablement to CMS faculty and staff on approved AI tools and automation practice through guidance, templates, reusable components, and short training sessions.

Business analysis and AI enabled operational support

  • Partner with CMS faculty and operational stakeholders to identify, clarify, and prioritize opportunities where AI-enabled tools can improve University processes and services.
  • Act as the business analysis bridge between faculty, technical teams, and operational stakeholders for AI-enabled initiatives by eliciting stakeholder needs, mapping current processes, defining functional and data requirements, documenting use cases, establishing measurable acceptance criteria, and ensuring solutions remain aligned with business needs, University policies, data governance requirements, and agreed success measures.
  • Identify and assess authoritative internal and external data sources required for AI solutions, evaluating accessibility, relevance, completeness, consistency, lineage, privacy constraints, and fitness for purpose; profile and validate the data, document quality and remediation requirements, and coordinate with Institutional Research, Information Technology, data owners, and faculty to prepare reliable datasets for development and testing.
  • Support the design, prototyping, testing, evaluation, and responsible adoption of agentic AI tools, including validation of outputs, workflow behavior, data use, and operational performance.
  • Develop supporting documentation, process maps, requirements specifications, data inventories, user guidance, and performance reports for AI-enabled initiatives.

Other Duties

  • Contribute to university-wide programs, including orientation, wellbeing initiatives, global observances, leadership development, and personal growth activities.
  • Perform all other duties as reasonably directed by the line manager that are commensurate with these functional objectives.

Qualifications and Criteria:

  • Bachelor's degree in statistics, data science, mathematics, computer science, information systems, business analytics, or related quantitative discipline.
  • Master's degree in a relevant quantitative, computing, mathematical, educational, or management discipline will be preferred.

Essential :

  • Minimum of six years of relevant experience in data analysis, academic analytics, business intelligence, institutional research, research analytics, or a closely related field, including at least two years spent building workflow automation or AI enabled solutions.
  • Demonstrated hands on experience designing, building, and operating automated workflows in a low code automation or data science platform such as KNIME or n8n, or a directly comparable tool such as Alteryx, Make, Zapier, Microsoft Power Automate, Dify, Flowise, or Apache Airflow. Candidates should be able to walk through workflows they personally built and maintained.
  • Practical experience building or configuring agentic AI workflows, meaning solutions in which a large language model uses tools, data sources, or multi step reasoning to complete a task, together with the ability to explain how the solution was tested, controlled, and handed over to users.
  • Practical comfort working with APIs, JSON, webhooks, scheduling, and authentication methods sufficient to connect systems reliably without full software engineering support.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing accurate reports and dashboards from multiple data sources and explaining findings to academic and professional stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in SQL and working proficiency in Python for data preparation, analysis, and automation, together with strong spreadsheet analysis skills.
  • Experience with a visualization platform such as Power BI or Tableau.
  • Professional fluency in English, with strong written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to elicit, analyze, and document business, functional, process, and data requirements in collaboration with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Working knowledge of applied AI concepts, including large language models, generative AI, prompt design, retrieval augmented generation, structured output, tool and function calling, agent orchestration, and common failure modes such as hallucination, prompt injection, and silent degradation over time.

Preferred :

  • Experience in a university or research-intensive environment, preferably supporting an academic division, college, department, or academic program.
  • Familiarity with student information systems, learning management systems, research information systems, data warehouses, survey platforms, and automated reporting workflows.
  • Knowledge of higher education data standards, academic quality processes, and the UAE higher education context.
  • Experience analyzing student outcomes, curriculum delivery, faculty activity, research productivity, or graduate education in computing, mathematics, or artificial intelligence disciplines.
  • Experience supporting the development or implementation of AI enabled operational tools, workflow automation, decision support solutions, or intelligent agents.
  • Experience with agent and AI development frameworks or platforms such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, Amazon Bedrock, or the developer platforms of major model providers.
  • Experience with embeddings, vector search, and retrieval design for document heavy or knowledge base use cases.
  • Familiarity with version control using Git, containerization, environment management, and basic deployment or CI/CD practice.
  • Relevant certification in an automation or analytics platform, for example KNIME, Alteryx, Power Platform, or a recognized AI engineering credential.
  • Exposure to AI governance, assurance, or risk management frameworks and their application to operational AI systems.

title: Sustainability Data Specialist
company: Bord Bia - The Irish Food Board
description:
Speisialtóir Sonraí Inbhuanaitheachta

Post Buan Lánaimseartha

Baile Átha Cliath

Speisialtóir Sonraí InbhuanaitheachtaAg obair faoi: Bainisteoir Anailísíochta Sonraí

Is ar an gcéad phointe den Scála a thosóidh Iontrálaithe Nua san Earnáil Phoiblí.

Cuspóir

Is é fís Bhord Bia go n-aithneodh custaiméirí ar fud na cruinne go bhfuil bia agus deoch na hÉireann ar chaighdeán domhanda; go bhfuil siad ar ardcháilíocht, sainiúil, agus á ndéanamh ag réimse éagsúil táirgeoirí cruthaitheacha ó ionad oileánda uathúil agus ámharach. Is é an cuspóir atá againn bia, deoch agus gairneoireacht den scoth na hÉireann a chur os comhair an tsaoil mhóir agus fás agus inbhuanaitheacht na dtáirgeoirí a chothú.

Sa ról seo, déanfaidh tú bailiú sonraí inbhuanaitheachta a bhainistiú, ar sonraí iad a chuireann ar chumas Bhord Bia éilimh agus pointí cruthúnais a fhorbairt agus tacú leo maidir le hinbhuanaitheacht bhia agus dheoch na hÉireann agus a léiríonn don tionscal go bhfuil inbhuanaitheacht tháirgí déiríochta agus mhairteoil na hÉireann ag feabhsú go leanúnach.

  1. Comhordú a dhéanamh ar bhailiú, ar chomhtháthú, ar bhailíochtú agus ar cháilíocht sonraí inbhuanaitheachta ar fud Scéimeanna Dearbhaithe Cáilíochta Bhord Bia agus an Chláir Origin Green.
  2. Tuarascálacha, deaiseanna agus léargais anailíseacha a fhorbairt lena ndéantar faisnéis fhiúntach as sonraí inbhuanaitheachta casta do pháirtithe leasmhara agus lena dtacaítear le cinnteoireacht fhianaisebhunaithe.
  3. Baint a bheith agat le forbairt agus le feabhsú modheolaíochtaí tuairiscithe inbhuanaithe agus réiteach sonraí inbhuanaitheachta a thacaíonn le Scéimeanna Dearbhaithe Cáilíochta Bhord Bia agus leis an gClár Origin Green.
  4. Anailís a dhéanamh ar phróisis ghnó, ar shreafaí sonraí agus ar cheanglais tuairiscithe ar fud Scéimeanna Dearbhaithe Cáilíochta Bhord Bia agus an Chláir Origin Green, agus deiseanna a shainaithint chun feabhas a chur ar cháilíocht sonraí, ar chumais tuairiscithe agus ar éifeachtacht an chórais.
  5. Oibriú le foirne teicniúla agus le soláthraithe seirbhíse chun tacú le cur i bhfeidhm na bhfeabhsuithe tuairiscithe, sonraí agus córais a fheabhsaíonn torthaí Scéimeanna Dearbhaithe Cáilíochta Bhord Bia agus an Chláir Origin Green.
  6. Comhordú a dhéanamh ar shruthanna oibre laistigh de AgNav agus ar thionscnaimh inbhuanaitheachta eile a thacaíonn le Scéimeanna Dearbhaithe Cáilíochta Bhord Bia agus an Chláir Origin Green.
  7. Sonraí inbhuanaitheachta, léargais anailíseacha agus aschuir tuairiscithe a chur i láthair páirtithe leasmhara inmheánacha agus seachtracha agus saineolas ar ábhar a chur ar fáil maidir le sonraí inbhuanaitheachta agus tuairisciú.
  8. Buiséid shannta a bhainistiú agus tacú le comhlíonadh RGCS, rialachais sonraí agus nósanna imeachta rialaithe Bhord Bia.
  9. Baint a bheith agat le tionscnaimh feabhsúcháin leanúnaigh agus le caighdeáin, beartais agus creataí rialachais Bhord Bia a chur i bhfeidhm ar na sonraí inbhuanaitheachta agus na gníomhaíochtaí tuairiscithe go léir.

Tú Féin

Taithí, Scileanna & Inniúlachtaí Riachtanacha

Taithí:

  • Beidh taithí 3-4 bliana i ról den chineál céanna ag an té a cheapfar.
  • Taithí ar thacair chasta sonraí a anailísiú agus a léirmhíniú chun léargais a ghiniúint, treochtaí a shainaithint agus chun tacú leis an gcinnteoireacht.
  • Taithí ar cheanglais ghnó a bhailiú, a anailísiú agus a dhoiciméadú chun réitigh tuairiscithe, anailíseacha agus sonraí a chur ar fáil.
  • Taithí ar thuarascálacha, deaiseanna, léirshamhlú sonraí agus aschuir thagarmharcála a fhorbairt do réimse páirtithe leasmhara.

Scileanna & Inniúlachtaí:

  • Cur chuige atá dírithe ar cháilíocht, an-aird ar mhionsonraí agus tiomantas do thascanna a chur i gcrích agus gealltanais a chomhlíonadh.
  • Cumas oibriú go héifeachtach le páirtithe leasmhara gnó agus teicniúla, agus tosaíocht a thabhairt do thionscadail iomaíocha chun sonraí, tuairisciú agus tionscnaimh a bhaineann le córais a chur ar fáil.
  • Sárscileanna, cumarsáide, anailíseacha agus réitigh faidhbe. Cumas coincheapa casta teicniúla nó anailíseacha a mhíniú go soiléir do lucht spéise neamhtheicniúil.

Is Fostóir Comhionannas Deiseanna é Bord Bia:

Sochaí inar comhionann gach duine atá uainn. Tuigimid gur riachtanach gur áit oibre chothrom a bheidh san fhondúireacht seo againne, áit a n-aithnítear gradam agus fiúntas gach duine agus a dtugtar an tsaoirse agus an deis dár bhfostaithe barr a gcumais a bhaint amach. Is mian linne go mbeidh tú in ann gach gné díot a féin a thabhairt chun na hoibre le gur fearr a bheidh tú in ann do dhícheall a dhéanamh agus do chuid cuspóirí a fhíorú agus tú ar thuras do ghairme linn. Tá údáil ár gcliant, custaiméirí agus margaí le feiceáil inár lucht saothair atá lán buanna agus lán éagsúlachta, agus baintear leas as réimse a gclint. Nuair a bhaintear gach leas as an réimse leathan dearcthaí atá ann mar gheall ar an éagsúlacht seo, cuirtear an nuálaíocht chun cinn agus cuidiú atá ann dúinn éirí níos fearr ó thaobh cruthaitheachta agus iomaíochta de.

Tá Bord Bia meáite ar rochtain chothrom iomlán a thabhairt do gach iarrthóir earcaíochta a oiread agus is praiticiúil é sin a dhéanamh. Má bhíonn aon tacaíocht nó socrú de dhíth ort sa phróiseas earcaíochta, déan teagmháil linn go díreach ag an seoladh humanresources@bordbia.ie

title: Data Governance Specialist - Informatica IDMC
location: Al Ruways Industrial City, United Arab Emirates
description:
Data Governance Specialist - Informatica IDMC

Location: Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates

Industry: I T and Services

Function: Information Technology

Experience: 4-8 years

Job Type: Full-time

Job Snapshot

Data Governance Specialist - Informatica IDMC in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates is an IT and Services opportunity for a data management professional with hands‑on experience in Informatica IDMC, data quality standards, governance frameworks, and enterprise data control practices. This role is ideal for a candidate who can implement data management solutions, improve data accuracy, support governance adoption, and work closely with business and technology teams in a fast‑moving digital environment.

Job Details

  • Country: United Arab Emirates
  • City: Abu Dhabi
  • Industry: I T and Services
  • Function: Information Technology
  • Salary: 18000-28000 (estimated)
  • Gender: Any
  • Candidate Nationality: Any
  • Job Type: Full-time

Role Context

The Data Governance Specialist - Informatica IDMC will help strengthen how enterprise data is managed, monitored, protected, and used across the organization. The position supports the implementation and maintenance of modern data management and governance solutions, with a strong focus on data quality, consistency, ownership, usability, and compliance. By working with technical teams, business users, data owners, and governance stakeholders, the specialist will help create reliable data practices that support better reporting, improved decision‑making, and long‑term digital maturity.

Key Responsibilities

  • Implement, configure, and maintain data management and governance solutions using Informatica IDMC and similar enterprise data platforms.
  • Support the development of data governance processes, workflows, controls, and operating procedures across business and technology functions.
  • Define, apply, and monitor data quality standards to improve accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, and reliability of enterprise data.
  • Work with cross‑functional teams to understand data issues, governance needs, system dependencies, and data ownership requirements.
  • Assist in building data quality rules, validation checks, metadata management processes, and data stewardship practices.
  • Review existing data management practices and recommend improvements to reduce duplication, improve governance visibility, and support trusted reporting.
  • Collaborate with data engineering, application, analytics, compliance, and business teams to ensure data is properly maintained and aligned with governance expectations.
  • Provide user guidance, training, and functional support on data management tools, governance standards, and data quality best practices.
  • Document governance processes, data quality rules, operating procedures, issue logs, and remediation actions.
  • Monitor industry trends, tool updates, and best practices in data management, data governance, and enterprise information control.
  • Support audits, governance reviews, and management reporting by maintaining clear documentation and evidence of governance activities.
  • Help promote a data‑aware culture by encouraging responsible data handling, better data ownership, and consistent use of approved governance procedures.

Ideal Profile

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Management, Business Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Proven experience implementing or supporting data management and governance solutions using Informatica IDMC.
  • Working knowledge of similar data management, data quality, metadata, cataloging, or governance toolsets.
  • Strong understanding of data quality concepts, governance operating models, data stewardship, metadata management, and data lifecycle practices.
  • Ability to translate business data needs into practical governance rules, workflows, and technical requirements.

title: Global PRP Program Manager (Remote - USA)
description:
Role Overview

PIC, a Genus PLC company, has an exciting opportunity. We are looking for a Global Pig Resistant Product (PRP) Program Manager (remote).

This role leads the integration, coordination, and governance efforts of PIC's global PRP program. As PRP expands across multiple markets with unique regulatory, commercial, stewardship, and stakeholder requirements, this role ensures the program operates as one coordinated system rather than a collection of independent workstreams.

The Global PRP Program Manager maintains a holistic view of the PRP program, continuously connecting people, priorities, decisions, and workstreams to ensure the program remains aligned, adaptable, and positioned for successful commercialization. The role enables department and workstream leads to focus on their core responsibilities by removing barriers, simplifying cross-functional coordination, and creating the operational discipline needed to successfully scale PRP globally.

The successful candidate can work in a culturally diverse, fast-paced environment and establish priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain accuracy. The candidate can work autonomously as well as collaboratively across functional teams, demonstrating strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills. Success is measured through cross-functional alignment, effective governance, timely execution, proactive risk management, commercialization readiness, organizational accountability, and the successful expansion of PRP across global markets.

This position is based remotely in the United States, with travel approximately of 10% domestically.

The salary range for this position is $126,500 - $153,000 USD annually. The salary provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. Genus considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate's work experience, location, education/training, and key skills.

You Will

  • Serve as the primary coordinator and integrator across all PRP workstreams, ensuring alignment and execution as a unified global program.
  • Build and maintain strong cross-functional partnerships & relationships across commercialization, regulatory, legal, stewardship, supply chain, product development, quality, marketing, franchise, and leadership teams.
  • Lead the governance framework and operating rhythm for the PRP program, including meetings, reviews, decision-making processes, and reporting structures.
  • Identify, assess, and proactively manage program risks, dependencies, resource needs, opportunities, and organizational barriers to execution.
  • Drive organizational accountability by tracking decisions, commitments, action items, approvals, and contractual obligations through completion.
  • Develop and maintain standardized governance tools, dashboards, templates, reporting, and operational processes to improve visibility and consistency across the program.
  • Own and continuously improve the cross-functional PRP Market Readiness Framework, ensuring commercialization readiness across global markets.
  • Coordinate commercialization planning activities, scenario evaluations, and cross-functional readiness efforts to support strategic decision-making and market expansion.
  • Monitor evolving regulatory, commercial, operational, and market conditions and ensure program plans adapt while maintaining organizational alignment.
  • Maintain a comprehensive view of program progress, strategic decisions, lessons learned, and key documentation, enabling effective communication and organizational learning.
  • Facilitate communication and coordination among global markets, franchises, consultants, customers, and internal stakeholders to ensure insights are incorporated into program strategies and priorities.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance governance, commercialization effectiveness, scalability, cross-functional collaboration, and overall program performance.

Requirements

Basic Qualifications (required):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, Project Management, Supply Chain or a related field.
  • Progressive years of experience in program management, commercialization, product development, operations, strategic planning, or related business functions.
  • Demonstrated success leading large, complex, cross-functional programs involving multiple functions, stakeholders, and business priorities.
  • Experience managing strategic business initiatives from planning through execution.
  • Proven ability to influence, align, and build effective working relationships across diverse teams without direct reporting authority.
  • Experience developing and managing governance frameworks, executive reporting, operating cadences, and decision-making processes.
  • Strong organizational, communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills with the ability to translate complexity into actionable plans.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and business impacts while proactively driving solutions.
  • Experience working within global organizations and coordinating activities across multiple regions, cultures, and functional teams.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to support strategic decision-making in a dynamic environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree (MBA, MSc, or related advanced degree).
  • PMP, PgMP, Lean Six Sigma, or other project/program management certification.
  • Experience within animal health, agriculture, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, healthcare, or other regulated industries.
  • Experience supporting global product launches, commercialization programs, or market expansion initiatives.

Business Overview

Genus is an agricultural biotechnology pioneer. We are a global FTSE 250 company, headquartered in the UK, and listed on the London Stock Exchange. Genus PLC has a presence in over 70 countries and a global workforce of over 3,000 employees and growing. We are a worldwide leader in porcine and bovine animal genetics, partnering with farmers to transform how we nourish the world – a mission that is important to a sustainable future.

PIC currently supplies over 70% of the world’s top pork producers. We directly employ people in 18 countries worldwide and our products are available in more than 50 countries across the globe. We are a diverse team, ranging from scientists to sales teams, production personnel to customer service, and are all united by a passion for producing nutritious, affordable pork and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Our vision is clear: Pioneering animal genetic improvement to help nourish the world.

Benefits Overview

At Genus, we offer a competitive salary. Benefits include health, dental, vision, FSA/HSA, long and short-term disability, 401K, tuition reimbursement, paid holidays and ETO (earned time off). This position will have opportunities for growth.

title: Lead Specialist: Metadata and Reference Data
description:
About Us

Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. Job Summary

The Metadata and Reference Data Lead Specialist will be responsible for strengthening the organisation’s Data Governance capability through the effective management of business Glossaries, Data Lineage, Reference Data and Metadata Standards. The role will support improved data understanding, ownership, consistency, traceability and control across the business.

Key Focus Areas

  • Data glossary development and maintenance.
  • Business and technical metadata management.
  • Data Lineage documentation and validation.
  • Reference Data Governance and control.
  • Data Ownership and stewardship support.
  • Critical Data Element Metadata enrichment.
  • Standards implementation and evidence management.
  • Data Quality support through clear definitions, rules and ownership.
  • Governance reporting and issue tracking.
  • Stakeholder engagement across business, Technology, Risk and Data teams.

Key Accountabilities

  • Develop, maintain and enhance the business data Glossary to ensure consistent definitions, terminology and business understanding.
  • Support the documentation of Data Lineage across key systems, reports, processes and Critical Data Elements.
  • Coordinate Reference Data reviews to ensure values, hierarchies, ownership, usage and controls are clearly defined and maintained.
  • Work with Data Owners, Data Stewards, Product Owners and System Owners to confirm definitions, lineage, rules and metadata requirements.
  • Support the identification and documentation of Critical Data Elements, including definitions, sources, usage, ownership and controls.
  • Maintain accurate Metadata records and ensure alignment to Data Governance standards.
  • Identify gaps in Metadata, Glossary, Lineage and Reference Data and track remediation actions.
  • Prepare governance updates, dashboards and reports on metadata, glossary, lineage and reference data progress.
  • Support audit, risk and regulatory evidence requirements relating to data traceability, ownership and control.
  • Contribute to the implementation of data management policies, standards and operating procedures.

Operational Effectiveness

  • Improve the completeness, quality and usability of metadata across priority data domains.
  • Ensure glossary terms, lineage and reference data artefacts are maintained accurately and timeously.
  • Drive consistent use of approved definitions and reference data across reports, systems and business processes.
  • Support the reduction of ambiguity, duplication and inconsistent interpretation of data.
  • Track actions, dependencies and issues to ensure timely delivery against agreed governance plans.
  • Support automation and tooling opportunities for metadata, lineage and reference data management.

Good Governance

  • Promote adherence to data governance, metadata, lineage and reference data standards.
  • Ensure clear ownership and accountability for key data terms, reference data sets and lineage documentation.
  • Maintain reliable audit trails for approvals, changes, decisions and evidence.
  • Support governance forums with accurate reporting and clear escalation of risks or issues.
  • Ensure metadata and reference data activities support regulatory reporting, risk management and data quality improvement.
  • Embed sustainable governance practices that can be evidenced and monitored over time.

Stakeholder Management

  • Partner with business stakeholders to define and validate glossary terms, business rules and data usage.
  • Work closely with Technology and Architecture teams to document technical metadata and lineage.
  • Engage Data Owners and Stewards to confirm ownership, accountability and approval of metadata artefacts.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Finance, Operations and Reporting teams to ensure data is consistently understood and controlled.
  • Facilitate working sessions to resolve definition conflicts, lineage gaps and reference data issues.
  • Communicate requirements clearly and provide practical guidance to stakeholders.

Qualifications and Education

Relevant diploma or degree Certification in Data Governance, Metadata Management, DAMA, Information Management, Data Quality or Data Architecture would be advantageous.

Field of Study

Preferred fields include: Data Management or Data Governance Information Management Information Systems Computer Science Business Analysis Risk Management or Compliance Business Administration Data Analytics or Reporting

Work Experience

  • 5 - 8 years’ experience in Data Governance, Metadata Management, Reference Data, Data Quality, business analysis, reporting, risk or Information Management.
  • Experience developing or maintaining a data glossary, business definitions, metadata repositories or data catalogues.
  • Experience with data lineage documentation across systems, reports, processes or data flows.
  • Exposure to reference data governance, including code sets, hierarchies, ownership and change control.
  • Experience working with Data Owners, Data Stewards, Technology teams and business stakeholders.
  • Experience in a regulated environment, preferably financial services or banking, would be advantageous.
  • Experience using tools such as Collibra, Informatica, Ataccama, Microsoft Purview, Power BI, Excel, SharePoint or similar platforms would be beneficial.

Competencies

  • Strong understanding of data governance principles.
  • Good knowledge of metadata, glossary, lineage and reference data concepts.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving ability.
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
  • Ability to translate technical data concepts into clear business language.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and follow through on actions.
  • Structured, disciplined and process-oriented approach.
  • Comfortable working across business, technology, risk and governance teams.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and SharePoint.
  • Experience with data governance or metadata tools would be advantageous.

Education

Bachelor`s Degrees and Advanced Diplomas: Business, Commerce and Management Studies

Our Story

At Absa, our story is not a single narrative. It’s thousands of individual journeys unfolding across Africa and beyond. From colleagues serving customers in local communities to teams shaping financial solutions across borders, Absa is built on people who bring their lived experiences, ambitions and perspectives into the workplace every day. Whether you’re starting your career, a seasoned leader or somewhere in between, your contribution is seen, valued and connected to something bigger. Our presence across Africa – which spans personal and business banking, corporate and investment banking, wealth and investment management, and insurance – exists because of the people that show up in their roles with purpose. Across Botswana, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia, our colleagues are shaping what Absa becomes in each market. Beyond the continent, teams in global offices and a technology hub support and extend the stories that prove that African talent can lead, influence and innovate on the global stage. At Absa, your story matters because progress is driven by human experience, not hierarchy. When people are enabled to bring their whole selves to work, they don’t just build careers. They help shape the future of Africa’s financial services landscape.

About us

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today's needs and transition to more sustainable solutions.

Job Purpose

The Specialist Pipeline Engineer is responsible for leading pipeline engineering activities for ADNOC Offshore projects executed under the Project Management Consultancy model. The role ensures that offshore and subsea pipeline systems are designed, reviewed, and executed in accordance with ADNOC requirements, international engineering standards, project specifications, HSE requirements, and schedule commitments throughout Concept, FEED, EPC, construction, installation, pre-commissioning, commissioning, and start-up phases.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Leadership

  • Lead and coordinate pipeline engineering activities for offshore oil & gas developments.
  • Manage a team of Pipeline Engineers, Senior Engineers and Designers.
  • Ensure engineering deliverables are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with project quality requirements.
  • Provide technical leadership and engineering solutions for complex offshore pipeline systems.
  • Review and approve:
    • Pipeline Design Basis
    • Pipeline Routing Studies
    • Hydraulic Analysis
    • Wall Thickness Calculations
    • Pipeline Stability Analysis
    • Expansion and Flexibility Analysis
    • On-bottom Stability
    • Free Span Analysis
    • Buckling Assessment
    • Crossing Studies
    • Pipeline Mechanical Design
    • Material Selection Reports
    • Stress Analysis
    • Pipeline Alignment Sheets
    • Pig Launcher & Receiver Design

  • Ensure compliance with ADNOC standards and applicable international codes including DNV, API, ISO and ASME.
  • Review EPC Contractor engineering deliverables and provide timely comments.
  • Monitor engineering progress against project schedule.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary interfaces with Process, Mechanical, Structural, Civil, Instrumentation, Electrical, Marine, Subsea, and HSE disciplines.
  • Participate in design reviews, HAZID, HAZOP, SIL, Constructability, Value Engineering and Risk Assessment workshops.
  • Support engineering change management and Management of Change (MOC) activities.

    • Tie-In
    • Hydrotesting
    • Dewatering
    • Drying
    • Gauging

Procurement Support

  • Review technical specifications.
  • Prepare and review Material Requisitions
  • Evaluate Technical Bid Evaluations
  • Support procurement of line pipes, valves, fittings, coatings, insulation, and subsea equipment.

HSE & Quality

  • Promote ADNOC's HSE culture and ensure engineering activities comply with project HSE requirements.
  • Ensure design complies with safety, operability, maintainability, and integrity requirements.
  • Participate in engineering audits, safety reviews, and lessons learned workshops.

Project Coordination

  • Coordinate with Client, EPC Contractors, Vendors, Classification Authorities, and third-party consultants.
  • Monitor project risks and recommend mitigation measures.
  • Support project reporting and management reviews.
  • Mentor junior engineers and develop technical capability within the engineering team.

Minimum Qualifications & Experience

Moving forward together

title: Open call: JET Research, Strategy & Engagement Consultants
company: Institute for Human Rights and Business
description:
Open call — rolling expression of interest

ROLE SUMMARY

  • Title:Just Energy Transition (JET) Research, Strategy & Engagement Consultants

  • Type: Rolling expression of interest, matched to consultancy engagements as they arise

  • Reporting to: IHRB's Head of Climate & Just Transitions Programme

  • Location: South Africa, Indonesia or Senegal; open to other locations for candidates with strong relevant experience, network and language fundamentals

  • Duration:Varies by engagement; opportunities in this cycle run to on or before 30 April 2027

  • Pay: Day rate consultancy; specific budget confirmed per engagement

The Institute for Human Rights and Business(IHRB) is building a pool of experienced consultants to support the closing phase of its Just Transitions Programme's work on Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) countries. We are looking to hear from thoughtful researchers, strategists and engagement practitioners with genuine depth in one or more JETP contexts - South Africa, Indonesia, and Senegal.

This is not a single fixed role. It is an open call: IHRB will draw on this pool to fill specific, time-bound consultancy engagements as they are scoped over the remainder of the current grant period, and to build relationships for future phases of this work. Not every expression of interest will lead to paid work in this cycle, but strong candidates will be kept on file and approached directly as needs arise.

We are looking for people who can bring one or more of the following:

  • rigorous policy and systems research in a fast-moving field, particularly where justice/human rights issues and private sector/economic activity intersect;

  • strategic judgement on how to sequence and frame engagement with senior stakeholders across business, finance, government and civil society;

  • hands-on experience designing or facilitating convenings, dialogues, or other engagement formats;

  • strong, accessible writing for funder, policy and public audiences;

  • deep, credible relationships within one or more of the three JETP contexts

ABOUT IHRB'S JUST TRANSITIONS PROGRAMME

IHRB’s Just Transitions Programme focuses on a central challenge: current climate action models are structurally misaligned – and this is undermining delivery. Decision-making remains top-down across sectors, financial systems misprice social risk, and practitioners lack awareness of usable, investable models. The result is an implementation gap, where ambition is rising but delivery is contested, delayed, or fragile – raising material risks for workers and communities, company operations, and the transition itself.

Our core contention is that climate action succeeds when governed as a social process, not just a technical or financial one. Embedding the rights and agency of workers, communities, and affected stakeholders into how decisions are designed, sequenced, and financed is not a moral add-on – it is a precondition for effective, investable climate action. This approach is grounded in international standards, including the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, which establish participation, accountability, and due diligence as baseline conditions.

IHRB works to shift practice through three interconnected approaches:

  • making risk visible – by demonstrating how social exclusion translates into financial and operational costs

  • making the possible tangible – by identifying real-world models and mechanisms, and translating them into operational insights for diverse practitioners

  • making change actionable – by convening and engaging business, finance, policy, and civil society in dialogue on shared challenges and emerging issues

IHRB'S WORK ON THE 'J' IN JETPs

As part of this broader Just Transitions Programme, IHRB has undertaken a focused stream of work on the just energy transition landscape and progress in JETP countries. JETPs were launched in 2021 at COP26 as a new model for mobilising climate finance in support of national-level energy transitions. IHRB’s “J in JETP” project clarifies how justice is being interpreted and applied in national JET investment and implementation plans, and provides practical guidance on how private sector engagement can support, rather than undermine, social outcomes.

This work began in South Africa, with a comprehensive mapping of actors and policies within the national just energy transition framework, investments and implementation plans, as well as a deeper dive into distributive justice and the role of business in the country's energy transition. This formed the foundation for a companion study in Indonesia, which is in-process and nearing completion. Senegal is a new addition to this comparative work, with a bounded scoping study now being initiated.

South Africa and Indonesia are both cases of an incumbent fossil industry being phased out and open questions about the sequencing for which green systems each country will transition-in to. Senegal is structurally different: a low-base renewables buildout with no comparable incumbent industry to phase out. Candidates should be comfortable working with, rather than flattening, this kind of structural nuance between contexts.

AREAS WHERE WE MAY NEED SUPPORT

Depending on capacity and how the remainder of the grant period develops, potential engagements may include:

  • desk research, actor mapping, or documentation review in Senegal's JET context;

  • support with stakeholder engagement or dissemination activities around published South Africa or Indonesia research;

  • contributions to comparative analysis across the three JET contexts;

  • support around COP31/32 as well as national dialogues and related convening activity;

  • other research, strategy or engagement work that fits an expression of interest closely enough to be worth scoping.

The specific scope, timeline and budget for any engagement will be confirmed directly with candidates whose expertise is a strong fit.

PERSON SPECIFICATION

Knowledge & skills:

  • Genuine depth in the unique energy systems, transition governance, and political economy landscapes of Senegal, Indonesia, and/or South Africa;

  • Strong understanding of business and human rights and responsible business frameworks and incentives/disincentives, and of distributive justice approaches to energy transitions;

  • Strong analytical and writing skills, able to translate complex material into clear outputs for funder, policy and public audiences;

  • Relevant language fluency for the context in question (in particular, Bahasa Indonesia and French), alongside strong written English;

  • Ability to work independently within a small, globally distributed team, and to deliver reliably against fixed, often compressed, timelines.

Experience:

  • A demonstrable track record of independent research, stakeholder engagement with seasoned experts and practitioners across business, finance, government, and civil society, as well as knowledge product development in a comparable policy space.

  • Candidates based outside South Africa, Indonesia or Senegal must bring correspondingly strong career experience, network, and language fundamentals from one or more of the three countries to justify the fit.

TIMEFRAME & CONTRACTING

  • Timeframe:Varies by engagement; opportunities under this call are expected to run as soon as possible and up to the 30th of April 2027

  • Contracting:Consultancy agreement, subject to UK law, agreed per engagement

  • Compensation:Day rate consultancy, in line with IHRB's standard rate, negotiated and confirmed per engagement.

title: Nuclear Safety Analysis Engineer – Recycling
description:
SHINE Technologies is seeking a Nuclear Safety Analysis Engineer for our used nuclear fuel (UNF) Recycling product line. The US has more than 95,000 metric tons of used nuclear fuel and nowhere to put it. This role develops and applies the nuclear safety analysis that lets us turn it back into energy: transient and accident analysis, dose analysis, process hazard analysis (HAZOPs, FMEAs, etc.), and integrated safety analysis that demonstrate the Recycling Pilot facility meets our safety goals and the regulator’s requirements, from preliminary design through licensing and into operation.

The job takes judgment as much as method. Safety analysis at SHINE is expected to be right, not merely conservative: the analyst chooses assumptions they can defend, understands where the margin is and what it costs, and tells the design team when a requirement is not earning its keep as clearly as when a hazard is under-controlled.

Hybrid work arrangement will be considered. Our key facilities are in Janesville, Wisconsin and Fitchburg, WI. Candidates may be asked to travel occasionally for team meetings or onsite engagements, depending on business needs.

The base salary range for this position is $100,000 - $150,000 per year plus a comprehensive compensation package. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location.


Specific duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Own the Safety Analysis

  • Perform system analyses of anticipated transients and postulated accidents to demonstrate that safety and licensing requirements are satisfied.
  • Perform nuclear calculations to determine the total amount of material at risk as input into release calculations, using industry-standard codes such as MCNP and SCALE.
  • Perform radiological and chemical dose calculations for normal and accidental releases.
  • Lead or support Integrated Safety Analysis (ISA) activities including hazard evaluations (e.g., HAZOP, FMEA), process hazard analyses (PHA), and accident sequence development.
  • Review Quality Classification Forms that determine whether equipment is credited in the safety analysis, and challenge classifications the analysis does not support.
  • Own the safety analysis documentation for the Pilot facility, including dose release calculations, HAZOP and FMEA reports, and the ISA Summary or its equivalent.
  • Perform hand calculations using first principles to support and validate analysis results.
  • Perform code benchmarking and validation analyses to support code qualification and methodology development.

Support Design and Licensing

  • Choose analysis assumptions that are defensible rather than merely conservative. Document the reasoning and quantify the margin they create.
  • Tell the design team where the analysis shows a requirement can be relaxed, as well as where a hazard needs more control.
  • Contribute to licensing documents for NRC (or DOE) review and approval that describe how the suite of nuclear analysis codes will be applied along with inputs, models, and correlations to establish the design bases.
  • Support the licensing team in responding to regulator questions on the safety analysis.

Success in the First Twelve Months:

  • The safety analyses needed for the Pilot facility construction permit application (or equivalent) are complete, with assumptions and margins documented.
  • The analysis has been used to remove or relax at least one requirement that could not be justified, with the reasoning documented.
  • Analysis methods and codes are qualified and documented to a standard the licensing team can carry to the regulator.

title: Specialist – HR System & Data
description:
To administer, support, and continuously improve the organization’s HR systems and workforce data environment, with primary responsibility for ERP HCM platforms. The role ensures reliable, accurate and secure employee data, effective reporting and analytics, controlled system changes, and seamless integration between HR and other applications.

The role works closely with HR process owners, Information Technology, Finance, external vendors, and business stakeholders to translate operational requirements into effective system solutions, strengthen data governance, and enable informed workforce decision-making.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES

1.HR System Administration and Operational Support

  • Administer and provide functional support for Oracle and/or SAP HR modules, including payroll-related data, absence, performance, recruitment, learning, and employee self-service, workflows, approval in accordance with approved HR policies and processes.
  • Provide the first line support to Investigate user incidents, determine root causes, and coordinate resolution with Information Technology, vendors, and relevant HR teams.
  • Maintain an organized log of incidents, service requests, system defects, resolutions, and recurring issues.
  • Provide functional guidance and timely support to HR users, employees, and managers.
  • Develop user guides, process documentation, frequently asked questions, and system support materials.

2.HR Data Management and Governance

  • Maintain the accuracy and perform regular data-quality reviews, completeness, consistency, and integrity of employee, position, organization, and other workforce data across HR systems.
  • Establish and maintain HR data definitions, validation rules, coding standards, ownership requirements, and data-maintenance procedures.
  • Coordinate data cleansing, migration, conversion, and validation activities during system implementations, upgrades, and organizational changes.
  • Support the maintenance of organizational structures, positions, reporting lines, job information, grades, cost centres, and workforce records within the system.

3.Dashboards, Reporting, Analytics and Information Management

  • Work with HR stakeholders to clarify reporting requirements and translate them into practical dashboards, reports, and data solutions.
  • Develop and maintain standard and ad hoc HR reports, dashboards, and workforce data extracts using Power BI, ERP, or approved business‑intelligence tools.
  • Provide accurate and timely workforce information covering headcount, turnover, vacancies, Emiratization, absence, employee movement, demographics, performance, and other HR indicators.
  • Validate reports against source-system records and reconcile discrepancies before information is released.

4.System Enhancement, Testing and Integration – 15%

  • Analyse, and document HR requirements for enhancements, automation, integrations, and initiatives.
  • Translate business requirements into functional specifications, process maps, configuration requirements.
  • Participate in system implementations, upgrades, and integration projects involving HCM, payroll, recruitment, performance, learning, time‑management, finance, and other enterprise systems.
  • Prepare and execute functional testing, system integration testing, and user‑acceptance testing.
  • Document test results, identify defects, coordinate corrective actions, and verify resolution.
  • Coordinate with Information Technology and vendors to ensure accurate and secure data exchange between integrated systems.
  • Support change implementation, user communications, training, and post‑go‑live stabilization.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify HR processes, reduce manual transactions, improve employee experience, and increase the use of automation and self‑service.

5.Security, Controls, Compliance and Documentation

  • Support the administration and periodic review of HR system access, user roles, approval authorities, and segregation‑of‑duties controls.
  • Ensure system access is granted, amended, and removed based on approved requests and assigned responsibilities.
  • Support internal and external audits by providing system records, data extracts, evidence, and responses.
  • Monitor compliance with applicable HR policies, information‑security requirements, data‑privacy.
  • Escalate material system, data, access, integration, or compliance risks to the Senior Director – HR.
  • Track agreed corrective actions arising from audits, data reviews, access reviews, or assessments.

4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES

Minimum Qualifications:

(Education/Certification/

Licensure/Professional Membership)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Management Information Systems, Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, Data Analytics, or a related discipline.
  • One or more of the following would be advantageous: Oracle HCM Cloud or Oracle E‑Business Suite certification.
  • IFS / SAP SuccessFactors or SAP HCM certification.
  • HR analytics or data‑management certification.
  • Business analysis, project management, or IT service‑management certification.
  • Power BI, SQL, or other reporting and analytics certification.
  • 5 years of relevant experience in HR systems, HR data management, HR reporting, or HR technology.
  • At least three years of hands‑on functional experience with IFS, Oracle HCM, Oracle E‑Business Suite, SAP HCM, and/or SAP SuccessFactors.
  • Experience supporting HR system implementation, configuration, testing, upgrades, integrations, or data‑migration activities.
  • Experience preparing workforce reports, dashboards, data reconciliations, and management information, system access controls, and audit requirements.
  • Aviation, engineering, manufacturing, MRO, or another regulated‑industry background would be advantageous.

Job Specific Competencies:

1. HR Systems and Digital Enablement

Demonstrates strong functional understanding of HR technologies, particularly IFS, Oracle and/or SAP, and applies this knowledge to support operations, configure solutions, automate processes, improve system usability, and enhance the employee and manager experience.

2. Data Governance and Analytical Thinking

Maintains accurate, complete, consistent, and secure HR data. Analyses workforce information systematically, identifies trends and discrepancies, and converts data into reliable insights that support management decision‑making.

3. Accuracy and Attention to Detail

Completes system transactions, configurations, reports, testing, and documentation with a high level of precision. Carefully verifies information, detects inconsistencies, and corrects errors before they affect employees, payroll, reporting, or business operations.

4. Problem‑Solving and Root‑Cause Analysis

Investigates system, process, and data issues logically to identify their underlying causes. Develops practical and sustainable solutions, evaluates potential impacts, and takes appropriate corrective or preventive action.

5. Customer and Employee Service Orientation

Responds promptly and professionally to system users and HR stakeholders. Understands their requirements, provides clear guidance, manages expectations, and delivers solutions that are practical, user‑friendly, and aligned with approved policies and processes.

6. Collaboration and Stakeholder Management

Builds effective working relationships with HR teams, Information Technology, Finance, system vendors, managers, and other stakeholders. Communicates requirements clearly, coordinates activities, and facilitates agreement on system, data, and process solutions.

7. Planning, Organization and Delivery

Prioritizes and manages multiple operational requests, reports, testing activities, system changes, and projects effectively. Meets agreed deadlines, follows through on commitments, and maintains proper documentation and progress tracking.

8. Confidentiality, Integrity and Accountability

Handles employee and organizational data with discretion and in accordance with applicable policies, access controls, and data‑privacy requirements. Takes ownership of assigned responsibilities, acts ethically, and promptly escalates errors, risks, or control concerns.

title: Data Specialist - Project - (6 Months)
description:
POSITION:

Data Specialist - Project 6 Months

LOCATION:

Epsom Downs, Johannesburg

REPORTING TO:

Director: Conservation Development

Purpose

Owns the organization’s data architecture across systems — starting with, but not limited to, the finance ERP — and actively drives the conversion of manual data capture into automated data capture wherever it makes sense to do so. Acts as custodian of financial data as the canonical source of truth, and builds the reporting, automation, and integration layer connecting the ERP to the rest of the organization’s systems. This is not a passive data-analysis role: a core part of the mandate is identifying where manual processes are introducing risk or wasted effort and building the automation to remove them.

Relationship to the Business Central Migration

This role is not the primary technical lead on the Business Central migration — that responsibility sits with the Microsoft Partner and Finance ERP Manager as day-to-day liaison. However, this role's involvement is still load-bearing, in three specific ways:

  • Owns the data architecture that replaces what Serenic's fund-accounting layer used to do. Business Central does not natively support funds, grant, or encumbrance accounting, so this logic must be rebuilt as a dimension structure. Designing how funds, cost centers, and restricted/unrestricted tracking get modelled is a data architecture problem and sits with this role. This is the single most concrete, highest-stakes piece of migration involvement it carries.
  • Owns the business logic behind anything builds on the company’s behalf, so that knowledge does not live only with the vendor. The intercompany elimination automation is the clearest current example: The Microsoft Partnerbuilds it, but this role is responsible for understanding why it works the way it does, so the organization is not permanently dependent on the vendor to explain its own system.
  • Pick up the integration and automation work that sits just outside the migration's Phase 1 boundary — connecting Kiss flow, Salesforce, and other systems to Business Central; building write-back budget reporting; eventually migrating Jet Reports to Power BI. None of this is "the migration" in the narrow sense, but all of it only becomes possible once the migration lands, and all of it is what turns a working ERP into a well-integrated one.
  • In short: the Finance ERP Manager keeps the migration moving day-to-day; this role makes sure it is being built on a data structure that will actually hold up.

Key Responsibilities

  • Owns and maintains a data map of the organization — what data lives where, and where it needs to flow between systems (the finance ERP, Kiss flow, Salesforce, ResRequest, TallOrder, Sage 300, Jet Reports, Power BI).
  • Acts as custodian of the ERP's financial data as the organization’s canonical source, guarding against corruption from manual entry and championing automation wherever possible.
  • Systematically identifies manual, repetitive, or error-prone data capture processes across the organization and assesses where converting them to automated capture is appropriate — this is an active, ongoing part of the role, not an occasional project. AP Reporter, an internal tool already used to digitize previously manual field data capture, is a useful illustration of the kind of work this role should be doing more broadly, including on the operational side of the business.
  • Designs and builds automation using Power Apps and Power Automate to replace manual workflows — for example, structured data-entry forms in place of ad hoc spreadsheets, or automated approval/routing steps in place of manual email chains.
  • Designs and builds Power BI dashboards and reports, in collaboration with the company'sBI team, including budget-vs-actual, compliance monitoring, and ad hoc analytical requests.
  • Builds ERP-integrated budget reporting with write-back capability (e.g. via a tool such as Velixo), replacing the current static, Excel-based annual budget process.
  • Owns the Phase 2 migration of existing Jet Reports functionality into Power BI — auditing existing reports, understanding their purpose and audience, and defining what should be rebuilt versus retired.
  • Leads the data-integration design for connecting adjacent systems to Business Central — including vendor master data ownership, dimension mapping for fund/cost-center tracking, and sync error handling (relevant to Kiss flow, Salesforce, and other integrations).
  • Designs the approach to historical data retention once the legacy ERP environment is decommissioned — e.g. extracting to a data lake (such as Microsoft Fabric) rather than keeping a live, costly legacy system running indefinitely.
  • Build training materials and dashboards that help operational users understand the quality and purpose of the data they capture, in partnership with the People & Change role.
  • Works closely with the existing in-house BI team, historically a separate, request-driven function with no direct working relationship with Finance.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Strong data architecture or data modelling background, ideally with exposure to ERP-centric environments.
  • Maintains comprehensive, up-to-date documentation and architecture diagrams of the data landscape — a mandatory, not optional, part of the role, given the succession risk inherent in such a specialized position.
  • Hands-on, practical experience building automation with Power Apps and Power Automate specifically — this is a core, not peripheral, requirement for this role.
  • Hands-on experience with Power BI and, ideally, Microsoft Fabric.
  • Experience integrating an ERP with adjacent business systems such as CRM, procurement, point-of-sale, or payroll platforms.
  • A genuine automation-first mindset — able to spot where a manual process should become an automated one, and to weigh that judgement against effort and risk, not just build automation for its own sake.
  • Working SQL proficiency.
  • Strong stakeholder management — this role sits across departments by design and needs to work with Finance, BI, Operations, and IT without a single clean reporting line.

Advantageous, Not Required

  • Direct experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
  • Experience with Excel-to-ERP reporting/write-back tools such as Velixo.
  • Experience with multi-entity consolidation or intercompany elimination design.
  • Nonprofit or donor-funded sector experience.
